correctness.rationale: Exact Dirichlet/Beta gap law and hyperbolic cosine rule give finite-sample expectation. Cubic-gap upper bound with exact moments proves subcritical convergence; deterministic Jensen bound proves supercritical convergence. Exponential-spacings coupling and O_p(n^-2) linearization error yield the critical law and nondegenerate triangular-array Gaussian CLT; integrable expansions justify endpoints and fixed-radius term. verify.py provides independent finite numerical corroboration, not universal certification.

value.rationale: The hyperbolic circle circumference grows exponentially. The theorem identifies the exact sample-resolution threshold n comparable to sinh R, supplies an explicit universal strictly monotone interpolation and positive Gaussian fluctuation variance at critical scaling, and recovers fixed-radius approximation rates as a consistency boundary. This answers a meaningful scaling/approximation problem rather than a routine substitution or finite census.
